content.comment_body: I'm experiencing a strange problem communicating with a [product_name]. When I connect my PC directly to the [product_name], everything works without any issues using [product_name] V[version_no]. However, if I connect via a switch (specifically a [product_name] dumb switch), the software cannot detect the device, although pinging it works fine. Interestingly, another [product_name] with version [version_no] on the same network connects successfully through the switch. Any advice?

Since the first [product_name] works with a direct cable and another [product_name] connects fine through the switch, this doesn't appear to be a standard hardware fault. As a troubleshooting step, I suggest connecting the cable and switch port used by the second [product_name] to the first one. If that works, it's likely that both devices are OK. You might also consider swapping the Ethernet cables to see if that resolves the issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter inconsistent network connectivity with [product_name] devices when using a switch. Direct connection from PC to a [product_name] works, but one device isn't recognized via switch while another with the same version is detected correctly. There is an expectation for reliable Ethernet detection and uniform network performance across all devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want both [product_name] devices with version [version_no] to connect reliably to the software using the network switch, ensuring consistent detection and communication.
